video_title: Domantas Sabonis switched agents, what does that mean for the Sacramento Kings?

quotes.speaker: James Ham
quotes.summary_phrase: Domantas Sabonis switching to CAA and agent Aaron Mintz
quotes.excerpt: Domantas Sabonis has left his longtime representation at Wasserman and has joined CAA led by Aaron Mintz.
quotes.quote: Domantas Sabonis has left his longtime representation at Wasserman and has joined CAA led by Aaron Mintz and company. Aaron Mintz is a longtime agent in the NBA. He has had plenty of clients here in Sacramento. You never really know what this means when a player switches agents, but Mintz has a track record for getting his players out of their current situation and into a new situation, typically armed with a new extension, a new extension in the place that they're going to.

quotes.speaker: James Ham
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst's take on Sabonis wanting out of Sacramento
quotes.excerpt: Brian Windhorst took a detour into the Sabonis situation in Sacramento. His response was he wants to get the hell out of Sac.
quotes.quote: During an episode of the Hoop Collective podcast last week, the trio of Anthony Slater, Tim McMahon, and Brian Windhorst took a detour into the Sabonis situation in Sacramento. Windhorst had one of those epiphany moments that he likes to have, and it has a lot of people talking. Windhorst then handed it over to Tim McMahon and asked, 'Why would he do that?' and his response to that was, 'He wants to get the hell out of Sac.'

quotes.speaker: James Ham
quotes.summary_phrase: Anthony Slater's clarification on Sabonis's extension eligibility
quotes.excerpt: Domantas Sabonis is extension eligible and the Kings are not interested in having that conversation.
quotes.quote: Anthony Slater later chimed in, 'Domantas Sabonis is extension eligible and the Kings are not interested in having that conversation.' Slater was also quick to add that Sabonis and Scott Perry have a very transparent, good relationship. Sabonis has recommitted to the Kings, but it always comes with the understanding that this relationship is probably not long for this NBA world.

quotes.speaker: James Ham
quotes.summary_phrase: Comparing Domantas Sabonis and Trae Young's defensive limitations
quotes.excerpt: They are all-star level players, but they don't fit every team, especially due to their weakness on the defensive end.
quotes.quote: The trio talked about the fact that Sabonis is similar in a lot of ways to Trae Young. They are all-star level players, but they don't fit every team, especially due to their weakness on the defensive end. I would add in their weakness on the defensive end and their gigantic salaries, which is something that Trae Young faces as well. The Kings, of course, had been offered Trae Young at one point in exchange for Zach LaVine. LaVine to Atlanta and Trae Young to the Sacramento Kings. The Kings said no to that deal from what I know, very specifically according to a source of mine. They said no because they knew that the second he got off a plane, he would want an extension and the Kings were not fully prepared to be in the long-term Trae Young business.

quotes.speaker: James Ham
quotes.summary_phrase: Sabonis's contract situation and injury recovery
quotes.excerpt: He has two years left and 95 million dollars remaining on his contract, but at 30, he's coming off a knee injury.
quotes.quote: One of the issues that the Kings have, and it's something that has stuck a couple of these deals, is that he has two years left and 95 million dollars remaining on his contract. But at 30, he's coming off a knee injury, and finding a team that is both willing to give up assets and extend him might not be in the cards. Any extension would start in his 32-year-old season, and he is very likely looking at a pretty substantial drop from his current salary, which again is 46 million this year and 49 million next, unless he bounces back fully healthy and maybe even adds a few things to his game.

quotes.speaker: James Ham
quotes.summary_phrase: Evaluating Keegan Murray and Jalen Duren as center prospects
quotes.excerpt: The Kings drafted a center last season in Keegan Murray, who showed an incredible amount of promise after his rookie season.
quotes.quote: There's also the fact that the Kings drafted a center last season in Keegan Murray, who showed an incredible amount of promise after his rookie season. They also added another rookie big man last year in Jalen Duren. Again, he turned heads with his defensive acumen and sort of his joy for the game of basketball. So whether the franchise believes that either of those guys are long-term solutions at center is unknown at this time, but this is at least a small part of the overall package.

quotes.speaker: James Ham
quotes.summary_phrase: Sabonis's potential to unlock Darius Garland's development
quotes.excerpt: I can make the case that Domantas Sabonis has the potential to completely unlock Darius Garland in the same way that I think Russell Westbrook helped to unlock Maxime Raynaud last season.
quotes.quote: I can make the case that Domantas Sabonis has the potential to completely unlock Darius Garland in the same way that I think Russell Westbrook helped to unlock Maxime Raynaud last season. Garland is used to playing with a rim runner. That's what he played in college at Arkansas. You can go back and look at his game film. He's a great lob thrower, but also he's used to that style of big man. That's not Domantas Sabonis, but playing with Sabonis will actually force Darius Garland to play off-ball. It will also force him to potentially learn the DHO game, the dribble-handoff game, where it's a big man directing traffic and not the guard. It's an inverted pick-and-roll, which the Kings used a couple of years ago.

quotes.speaker: James Ham
quotes.summary_phrase: Developing Keegan Murray and Jalen Duren through Sabonis's skills
quotes.excerpt: I also like the idea of Keegan Murray and Jalen Duren learning some of the skills that Sabonis has.
quotes.quote: I also like the idea of Keegan Murray and Jalen Duren learning some of the skills that Sabonis has. So again, one of the problems the Kings have had in the past is that when you have Sabonis, you start running this specific style of offense. When Sabonis steps off the court, it goes to hell in a handbasket. You have no idea how to adjust, or the Kings have not been able to adjust. It's almost like you have to have two separate offensive sets, one for when Domos is on the floor and one for when he's off the floor. And that's again more because the Kings have never gone out and found a big man who can move the ball like Sabonis. Now, that may have changed this week when the Kings brought in Ben Simmons, but we still have to see if Ben Simmons can, can get back on the court and can actually hold up and do some of the things that he's done in the past.

quotes.speaker: James Ham
quotes.summary_phrase: Scott Perry's meeting with Jalen Duren in Miami
quotes.excerpt: Scott Perry went and had a dinner with Jalen Duren in Miami early in free agency.
quotes.quote: Scott Perry went and had a dinner with Jalen Duren in Miami early in free agency. I will tell you, if you're Jalen Duren and his representative, I would look at the Sacramento Kings and know they can get up to max cap space next summer. Zach LaVine is coming off the books. Scott Perry is completely turning the franchise over, and I can tell you he has Jalen Duren's name in highlighter pen looking at next summer's free agency, if Duren is willing to take the qualifying offer.

quotes.speaker: James Ham
quotes.summary_phrase: Detroit's contract offer to Jalen Duren
quotes.excerpt: Detroit currently has an offer on the sheet in the neighborhood of 30 million per season per reports.
quotes.quote: Detroit currently has an offer on the sheet in the neighborhood of 30 million per season per reports. There's even some reports now that that offer may have gone up closer to 35 million, but Duren is looking for 40 plus million. And it gets a little complicated. A sign and trade, I think it's the most the Kings could offer is a four-year 176 million dollar deal. So that's basically the equivalent of an average salary of I think 44 million dollars a year. Am I wrong? Is my math wrong? Something like that. That's the most the Kings could offer. The Pistons can offer up to five year. They can actually go up to like 183 million, something like that. I don't think he's getting that type of money, but this is because he made the All-Star team. And so it bumps up what his percentage of the salary cap that he can get as an extension.
